Save
Berkshire Hathaway Inc. spent about $9.6 billion to buy back its own shares in the third quarter, a sign the company’s executives viewed the stock as undervalued. But declining insurance underwriting weighed on its operating earnings in a mixed quarter for the company.
The Omaha, Nebraska-based conglomerate’s operating earnings fell to $12.7 billion in the third quarter, a 5.8% decline from a year earlier, it said Saturday in a statement. Insurance underwriting declined by 43%, as its auto insurer Geico faced an increase in losses and a surge in underwriting expenses over the period. The firm’s insurance net investment income also declined 14% to $2.7 billion, largely because of lower short-term interest rates.

item.title: How the Iran War Is Making Alaskans Both Richer and Poorer
item.description:
Wall Street Week • Nov 7th, 2026
How the Iran War Is Making Alaskans Both Richer and Poorer
Oil prices have surged across the United States as a result of the ongoing war in Iran. This means higher costs for households in most states, but in Alaska, the state government is bringing in new revenue from its high oil production to offset those higher costs. Some of the revenue is then redistributed to Alaskans through the state’s unique sovereign wealth fund. While most Americans disapprove of the war in Iran, Alaska may emerge as a quiet winner from one of the conflict’s most painful economic side effects: higher oil prices.

Animal health companies are tapping into the protein craze, investing billions of dollars to build up businesses focused on making cattle, pigs and poultry healthier for human consumption.
A growing global population and changing consumer habits have boosted protein consumption, with accelerated US demand driven by weight-loss drugs and renewed government emphasis on meat in their diets. That has opened up opportunities for pharmaceutical firms and investors to pursue technologies to make livestock healthier and improve efficiencies on the farm.

Turkish authorities arrested the former deputy chairman of the country’s markets regulator, state-run Anadolu Agency reported on Saturday, the latest executive to be caught up in a widening fund scandal.
A court ordered the arrest of Enver Usca on bribery charges, Anadolu reported, without citing a source for the information. Usca’s four-year term at the regulator, known as the SPK, ended on Oct. 31.

item.title: Trafigura Snaps Up Copper in Asia as China Faces Supply Crunch
